summary:
I built JKMODE.EXE, the per-box display-mode helper for Jedi Knight DF2 (JK.EXE 1.01) and Mysteries of the Sith (JKM.EXE). It is built and the Linux-side tests pass, but it has never run on Windows. Wine is not installed and the build VM was down.

What it does:
- It repeats each game's own enumeration: DirectDrawEnumerateA, then per device DirectDrawCreate, pass 1 SetCooperativeLevel (0x51 for DF2, 0x11 for MotS) with EnumDisplayModes keeping only 320-wide modes, then pass 2 SetCooperativeLevel(0x11) with EnumDisplayModes keeping everything. Both passes share one counter capped at 64, followed by SetCooperativeLevel(8), QueryInterface(IID_IDirect3D) and EnumDevices (4 at most).
- It picks the same (device, 3D device) pair the game stores when a player ticks "3D Acceleration". That is the game's load-routine selection: an add-on 3D card is preferred (for example a Voodoo 2 behind a 2D card), otherwise the first device passing the HAL / perspective-texture / z-buffer / RGB / 16-bpp test.
- It writes displayDeviceGUID and 3DDeviceGUID (16 bytes each), displayMode = the index of WxH at 16 bpp, and b3DAccel=1. It uses REG_BINARY because that is what the game writes, then reads every value back.

Corrections and additions to the verified entries (found in the disassembly):
- displayMode and b3DAccel are REG_BINARY 4 bytes, not DWORD.
- The game never range-checks displayMode (JK 0x414ba6, MotS 0x41751f). A stale index past the end of the list reads beyond the array.
- If the key's Version value is present and not "0.1", the game deletes the whole key at start-up (RegDeleteKeyA at 0x50f254). JKMODE refuses in that case.
- The primary display driver's GUID is stored as 16 zero bytes. List entry 0 is a "Window Display Device" with its own constant GUID.
- Only one of these changes the design (stale index); the rest confirm the verified analysis.

When it refuses and writes nothing:
- The mode is not in the game's 64-entry list (exit 3). The report gives the uncapped position, for example "offered at position 76 of 78" on .240.
- No 3D device passes the game's test (exit 4).
- Enumeration fails where the game's own list build would also fail (exit 2).
- The Version value would make the game wipe the key (exit 5).
- Exit 6 means a registry write or delete did not read back as written.
- On a refusal it removes only a stored displayMode that is past the end of the list the game will use, together with b3DAccel. That returns the game to its first-start defaults. A player's manual in-range choice is never touched.

Build: CRT-free mingw i686, -march=pentium with no SSE or cmov. It imports only KERNEL32, USER32 and ADVAPI32, loads ddraw.dll dynamically, and has no .rsrc and no manifest. The missing manifest is deliberate: under UAC the helper is registry-virtualized exactly like the unmanifested games. Subsystem version is 4.0. The build is deterministic: two builds give the same md5, 19a53200a436ac427f7351b1af654608 (12,288 bytes). The COM vtable offsets and stdcall callback return sizes in the binary match the game's.

apply.py --check passes (rc=0): the staged JK.EXE and JKM.EXE match md5 and size, 26 and 25 asserted instruction/constant offsets hold, and install.reg creates exactly the key JKMODE writes. JKMODE.EXE, the Play .bats and FLEETRES are not staged yet. apply.py --build produced the helper plus a manifest and reference launchers. No game file is patched. The helper was not run on any box and nothing was written to the share.
launcher_changes_needed: scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py, TITLES: add "JediKnightDF2" and "JediKnightMotS" entries. Each gets a "new" launcher and a "launch_txt" row (neither title has a Play .bat today; launch.txt points straight at the exe), and payload() must stage FLEETRES.EXE/FLEETRES.BAT into both trees. new_launcher() needs a JK branch (for example `if title in ("JediKnightDF2","JediKnightMotS")`) that emits a NEW_JEDI template. The exact expected text is provisioning/patches/jk-helper/apply.py launcher_text(title), and the generated reference files are ~/.retro-fleet/patch-out/jk-helper/<Title>/<launcher>. Keep the generator and apply.launcher_text() in step; tests/python/test_patch_jk-helper.py pins the latter.

Files/Games-Library/JediKnightDF2/Play Jedi Knight.bat (new, CRLF). The functional lines, in this order: `cd /d "%~dp0"` / `call "%~dp0FLEETRES.BAT"` / `if exist "%~dp0JKMODE.EXE" "%~dp0JKMODE.EXE" df2 %FR_W% %FR_H% > "%~dp0JKMODE.LOG" 2>&1` / `start "" JK.EXE` / `exit`
Files/Games-Library/JediKnightMotS/Play Mysteries of the Sith.bat (new, CRLF): the same, with `"%~dp0JKMODE.EXE" mots %FR_W% %FR_H% > "%~dp0JKMODE.LOG" 2>&1` and `start "" JKM.EXE`

JediKnightDF2/launch.txt line 0: `JK.EXE<TAB>Jedi Knight - Dark Forces II<TAB>JK.EXE` becomes `Play Jedi Knight.bat<TAB>Jedi Knight - Dark Forces II<TAB>JK.EXE`. The display name and icon are unchanged, so the .lnk keeps its name and icon.
JediKnightMotS/launch.txt line 0: `JKM.EXE<TAB>Jedi Knight - Mysteries of the Sith<TAB>JKM.EXE` becomes `Play Mysteries of the Sith.bat<TAB>Jedi Knight - Mysteries of the Sith<TAB>JKM.EXE`

Stage JKMODE.EXE into both trees with `python3 provisioning/patches/jk-helper/apply.py --publish` (sharewrite put, one file at a time, verified). Alternatively stage-fleetres.py payload() can copy it, as it does FLEETRES.EXE; pick one owner, not both.

Use FR_W/FR_H, not FR_W43/FR_H43. The user wants 1920x1080. If the hardware check shows the 4:3 Sith renderer stretched unacceptably at 16:9, switch the JKMODE argument to `%FR_W43% %FR_H43%`. JKMODE refuses cleanly if that mode is not in the list; 1440x1080 is not in most of these drivers' lists.

GAMERES (agent/shared/gameres.h): NO rule for these titles, deliberately. The value is an index that only a DirectDraw enumeration on the box can produce, so it belongs in the launcher, and GAMESYNC's install.reg merge does not touch these values. Nothing in the agent must write displayMode.

provisioning/fleetres/PER-TITLE-STATUS.md rows JediKnightDF2 and JediKnightMotS (fleetres owner): change 'incapable' to '1080p via JKMODE.EXE (per-box index) on .123/.145/.195; .240 refused - 1920x1080x16 enumerated at 76, past the 64-entry list', once verified on hardware.

After every lane has published: bump Files/Games-Library/_deploy_generation.txt ONCE (scripts/fleet/autodeploy.py), or no provisioned box re-syncs these titles. Then run scripts/validate-staged-library.py.
tests:
`python3 -m pytest -q tests/python/test_patch_jk-helper.py`: 31 passed, 0 skipped. The share was mounted and mingw was present; the evidence is .claude/evidence-1080p/build-jk-helper/pytest.txt.

What the tests cover:
- jklogic.h, the exact header jkmode.c includes, compiled natively with gcc -Werror and driven by a probe:
  - bpp mapping (PAL8 -> 8, RGB -> bit count, neither -> -1).
  - The per-box index from the four MEASURED mode lists (fixtures from ddenum): DF2 = 45 on .123, 34 on .145 and 58 on .195; .240 is cut, offered at 76 with only 64 kept.
  - The MotS model: 43 on .123, which has no ALLOWMODEX pass; .240 cut; .145 listed.
  - The cap is exactly 64 (entry 63 kept, the 65th dropped); pass 1 keeps only 320-wide modes, and the ModeX copy is never matched; only 16 bpp matches.
  - The D3D record test: a HAL is usable; an emulator is not (HW colour model 0), and neither is a device lacking DDBD_16, MONO-only, lacking a z-buffer, or lacking perspective textures. The add-on extra test (alpha, r14, r18) is covered.
  - At most 4 D3D devices; a HAL enumerated fifth is invisible.
  - The selection: primary HAL behind the emulators; an add-on card preferred; an add-on failing the extra test loses; loop 2 fallback; no usable device leads to a refusal.
  - The default device, GUID resolution, and stale-index detection.
- Source-to-table pins: per-game coop flags and registry keys in jkmode.c match apply.TITLES; the header caps match the asserted instruction bytes; the IID matches; REG_BINARY writes with sizes 4 and 16; the Version check comes before any write.
- apply.py pure logic: PE VA-to-offset mapping and byte verification on a synthetic PE, including negative cases; offset-table sanity; launcher house rules (no parentheses, CRLF, cd -> FLEETRES -> JKMODE -> start, launch.txt line under 1023 bytes); a detector test for parentheses.
- Windows build: two builds are byte-identical; imports are exactly KERNEL32/USER32/ADVAPI32; no .rsrc; subsystem version at most 5; no xmm/cmov/fcomi; the ddraw exports are named as strings for GetProcAddress.
- Share: the staged originals pass check_exe, and cmd_check returns 0.

Commands run:
- `apply.py --check` returned rc=0.
- `apply.py --build` returned rc=0 (JKMODE.EXE md5 19a53200a436ac427f7351b1af654608, 12,288 bytes).
- By hand: `objdump -p` (imports) and a scan of the vtable calls (SetCooperativeLevel +0x50 ×5, EnumDisplayModes +0x20 ×2, GetCaps +0x2c, QI +0, EnumDevices +0x10, Release +8) and stdcall rets (0x10/0x08/0x18). All match the game's COM calls.

Not run: JKMODE.EXE has never executed on Windows (no wine, build VM down, boxes off-limits in this phase).

Unrelated: tests/python/test_patch_descent3.py::test_build_and_publish_dry_run_against_a_fake_library fails on its own; that is another builder's area.
risks: It has never run on Windows. The COM call sequence, the vtable offsets and the stdcall callbacks match the game statically, but the first execution will be on a box. Do a dry run first: `JKMODE df2 1920 1080 dry list`.

The Sith renderer is 4:3. At 1920x1080 the picture may be horizontally stretched (unverified). The fallback is FR_W43/FR_H43, but most of these drivers do not list 1440x1080, so JKMODE would then refuse.

16-bit D3D at 1920x1080 has never been run on these cards. A driver that lists the mode may still fail to create a 16-bpp D3D surface or z-buffer at that size (VRAM). The game would then error or fall back; JKMODE cannot know this from the enumeration.
.195 (Win7): whether the legacy IDirect3D (v1) HAL passes the game's test is unverified. If it does not, JKMODE refuses with exit 4 and changes nothing.

.240: 1920x1080x16 is at position 76. JKMODE refuses every launch by design, so the title stays at whatever is stored there. Reaching 1080p on .240 needs a smaller driver mode list or a JK.EXE/JKM.EXE callback patch. Neither is built here.

Multi-adapter boxes: JKMODE, like the game's own 3D checkbox, prefers an add-on 3D DirectDraw device. On .143 (GeForce 6800 plus a V5 5500) or a Voodoo 2 box, that routes the game to the 3dfx card and its output, which may have no monitor. This is the game's own behaviour, not a new one, but check it on .143 before pushing there.

Every launch takes a DirectDraw EXCLUSIVE|FULLSCREEN cooperative level on a hidden 1x1 window for a moment. ddenum did the same on all four LCD boxes without changing the mode, but on Win7 it may flicker or briefly suspend DWM.
The index depends on today's driver list, and it is recomputed every launch. A clean in-game Quit also rewrites the same values, which is harmless.

The launcher uses %~dp0, cd /d and start "" (cmd.exe dialect). As with every staged Play .bat, it is unverified on Win9x/COMMAND.COM, although JKMODE.EXE itself imports only Win95-safe APIs and has no CRT.
A failed JKMODE is visible only in JKMODE.LOG beside the exe (RESULT REFUSED/FAILED lines). The launcher still starts the game, which then keeps its stored values.
hw_verification_plan:
Prerequisites:
- JKMODE.EXE, FLEETRES.EXE/BAT, both Play .bats and both launch.txt changes are staged.
- Each LCD box has been purged (`rd /s /q C:\Games\JediKnightDF2`, the same for MotS, plus their .lnk) and re-synced with GAMESYNC. Quote failed_files==0 and titles_total == the library count.
- Before anything, `REGREAD HKLM Software\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\v1.0` and the MotS key, and save both.

1. Dry run on each of .123, .145, .195 and .240:
   - `EXEC "C:\Games\JediKnightDF2\JKMODE.EXE" df2 1920 1080 dry list`, then the same with mots in the MotS dir.
   - Expected for DF2: .123 idx 45, .145 idx 34, .195 idx 58, and .240 "REFUSED ... position 76 of 78" (exit 3).
   - Expected for MotS: .123 idx 43.
   - Check that the 3D line names the HAL as usable, and that nothing changed in the registry (REGREAD again).
2. Real launch through the shortcut path. The Play .bat has no parentheses, so the agent can start it:
   - `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\JediKnightDF2" "Play Jedi Knight.bat"`.
   - `DOWNLOAD C:\Games\JediKnightDF2\JKMODE.LOG`. It must end `RESULT OK 1920x1080 16bpp 3D, displayMode=<idx>, 4 value(s) changed`, or `0 value(s) changed` on a second launch.
   - REGREAD must show displayMode = that index as REG_BINARY, b3DAccel=01000000, and the two GUIDs.
3. In-game proof, keyboard-navigable:
   - MotS is the screenshot-able proxy on XP (16-bit GUI). Esc, then Players Ok at 558 449, Setup at 544 409, Display at 318 99. The 3D Acceleration box must already be TICKED and the selected Available Video Modes row must be '1920x1080 16bpp'.
   - Enter a level. A fullscreen SCREENSHOT 0 on XP must show 1920x1080 3D. Record whether it is stretched; if it is unacceptable, switch the launcher to FR_W43/FR_H43.
   - DF2: same check, but its GUI is 8-bit and photographs with confetti colours; judge the geometry and the log.
   - .195 (Win7) cannot be photographed fullscreen. Use JKMODE.LOG, REGREAD, and DISPLAYCFG get while the game runs (expect 1920x1080).
4. .240: JKMODE.LOG must say REFUSED with position 76; the game starts on its stored or default mode; no registry change.
5. .143, only if the title is deployed there: dry run first. If it picks the V5 5500 as the add-on device, stop and decide before a real launch.
6. Leave each box clean:
   - Quit the game properly (Quit writes the same values) or taskkill `/im "JK.EXE"` / `/im "JKM.EXE"`.
   - After a taskkill, restore the desktop with ChangeDisplaySettings(NULL,0) (regmode.c) and confirm DISPLAYCFG get = 1920x1080.

What must NOT change: the DirectPlay LAN join. Host on .123 and join from .145 via TCP/IP with a blank Locate Session. Take screenshots of both, the same as the 2026-08-31 proof. Also unchanged: CD Path, InstallType and Version in HKLM; the desktop mode after exit; icons and launch.txt display names.
review_notes:
I built what titles-verified.json concluded (Route 2), with four refinements from the disassembly:
- The values are REG_BINARY (4 and 16 bytes), not DWORD.
- displayMode is never range-checked. So on a refusal JKMODE removes an out-of-range stored index plus b3DAccel, which restores the game's defaults, and nothing else.
- A Version other than "0.1" makes the game delete its key, so JKMODE refuses in that case.
- The recommended 3D device is exactly the pair stored when "3D Acceleration" is ticked (JK 0x414f87, MotS 0x41793a). The two-loop selection with the add-on preference is reproduced, not simplified to "first HAL".

Fixture approach for MotS: its first pass enumerates the NORMAL list's 320-wide modes. This reproduces the verifier's 43 on .123 and the hardware-observed .240 cut and .145 listing.

The helper is our own code (commit-able); no game bytes are in git. The fixtures are our own ddenum measurements.

Not done in this phase, by rule: nothing was run on a box, published, committed or pushed.
